title: Asthma in a child: control and attacks
what: A guide for parents: how to help a child with asthma every day and what to do during an attack.
why: If your child was found to have asthma or often has wheezing.
duration: a plan is made at the visit; treatment is usually long-term
tell_doctor: How often your child coughs at night or struggles to breathe
What triggers attacks: colds, dust, animals, running
How often the quick-relief inhaler is needed
How your child uses the inhaler: show the doctor

prepare.title: Spacer
prepare.text: Young children usually take the inhaler through a spacer with a mask. Ask your doctor which one fits.

prepare.title: Plan
prepare.text: Ask for a written action plan and give a copy to the kindergarten or school.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Less dust, and no smoking at home or in the car.

steps: Give the daily controller treatment as your doctor prescribed
Signs of an attack: cough, wheezing, fast breathing, the child cannot talk or play
Sit your child up and keep them calm
Give puffs of the quick-relief inhaler through the spacer, as in the plan
If there is no improvement, follow the red zone of the plan and call emergency services
Write down when the attack happened and what helped
feel: Your child may be afraid of the mask, so play with it beforehand
After the inhaler, a racing heart and restlessness are possible and usually pass
after: See your doctor for scheduled check-ups
Check the expiry date and how much is left in the inhalers
Do not stop the daily treatment on your own
red_flags: Your child has trouble breathing, or the skin between the ribs pulls in: call emergency services
Blue lips, or your child is limp or drowsy: call emergency services
The inhaler does not help: call emergency services

faq.q: Will asthma go away with age?
faq.a: In some children symptoms get milder. Only a doctor should decide to stop treatment.

faq.q: Can a child with asthma do PE?
faq.a: Usually yes, if asthma is well controlled. Talk to your doctor and give the school the plan.

reminders.text: Check that your child's inhaler and spacer are with you.
